- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- After a price spike, model tends to overshoot and then gradually correct — but often lags the true mean reversion.
- Model underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, particularly when true prices show a downward trend or mean reversion.
- When history shows strong upward momentum, model overreacts with a sharp spike followed by overcorrection.
- Model fails to capture short-term volatility in the last 5–10 days, often smoothing out true price drops or spikes.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher prices, especially when recent history is volatile or trending upward.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of price corrections after spikes — often missing the true “reversion to mean” phase.
- Model tends to overfit recent high prices, leading to overestimation when true prices are consolidating or declining.
